newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Rashid to buy stake in Indonesia bank.
newsitem.headline: Rashid to buy stake in Indonesia bank.

text.p: Malaysian stockbroking group Rashid Hussain Bhd said on Wednesday it has agreed to acquire a 20 percent stake in P.T. Bank Niaga of Indonesia for 234.47 billion rupiah in cash.
Rashid said in a statement that the acquisition will be funded by internal funds and borrowings.

Bank Niaga, a commercial bank, has a network of 41 branches and 18 sub-branches throughout Indonesia's major cities. It also provides other financial services such as securities underwriting and brokerage.
For the nine months ended September 30, 1996, the bank reported a net income of 71 billion rupiah.

Rashid said the acquisition would enable the group to develop and make significant in-roads into the Indonesian market. Rashid already has a stockbroking subsidiary, P.T. Rashid Hussain Securities, operating in Indonesia.
Rashid also announced a proposed acquisition of an additional 12 percent stake in Straits Asset Holdings Sdn Bhd, an investment holding company, for 33.49 million ringgit cash.

The additional stake would increase Rashid's equity interest in Straits Asset to 63 percent. Straits Asset owns stockbroking firm Straits Securities Sdn Bhd and financial futures broker Straits Futures Sdn Bhd.

Rashid said in line with the proposed corporate restructuring of the group, it has offered the 20 percent stake in Bank Niaga and the additional 12 percent interest in Straits Asset to 20 percent-owned associate DCB Holdings Bhd at the same purchase price to be satisfied by the issue of new DCB Holdings shares at 8.11 ringgit each.
Under the proposed restructuring exercise, Rashid's stake in DCB Holdings will be increased to 54.17 percent.
